seo.title: LTX 2.5 Fast AI Video Generator for Rapid Iteration
seo.description: Use LTX 2.5 Fast for current text, image and source-audio iteration, with practical duration and resolution limits, prompt advice and live canonical quotes.

overview: LTX 2.5 Fast is the current speed-oriented route for visual exploration, motion tests and draft iteration in the LTX family. Lightricks owns LTX; MaxVideoAI distributes this launch integration through Fal. The route supports text-to-video, image-to-video and a distinct audio-to-video workflow driven by a source audio asset.

hero.title: LTX 2.5 Fast
hero.subtitle: Iterate from text, an opening image or source audio, with native 720p through 4K tiers and duration choices suited to rapid review.
hero.paragraph: Choose Fast while the team is exploring motion, pacing, framing or prompt variations. Text and image modes support several output tiers and native generated audio; audio-to-video is a separate workflow priced from the validated source-audio duration. Lightricks is the model owner and Fal distributes execution for this release.

features.title: Fast prompt exploration
features.body: Use a six-second 720p pass to compare motion language, composition and subject behavior before committing to a higher-resolution or longer render. Keep each variant tied to one measurable change.

features.title: Native high-resolution tiers
features.body: Text and image generation can move through 720p, 1080p, 1440p and 4K. The higher tiers and high frame-rate choices have shorter duration ceilings, so review the active constraints before queuing.

features.title: Image-led movement tests
features.body: Animate a trusted opening frame and optionally guide the ending frame. Describe camera motion and physical change rather than restating the source image as a new composition.

features.title: Source-audio performance
features.body: Audio-to-video requires a private source-audio asset and can optionally use an image. The canonical quote uses server-validated input-audio duration, never an invented output duration supplied in editorial copy.

decisionCards.title: Best fit: fast creative iteration
decisionCards.body: Pick Fast for prompt A/B tests, social framing, motion studies and early storyboard beats where learning speed matters more than final-delivery positioning.

decisionCards.title: Not ideal: default final approval
decisionCards.body: When the concept is locked and the review calls for the production-oriented LTX sibling, move the same brief to Pro and compare the result deliberately.

decisionCards.title: Prompt one variable at a time
decisionCards.body: Hold subject, setting and style constant while changing camera, action or pacing. That discipline turns a fast render loop into useful production evidence.

referenceWorkflows.title: Text draft
referenceWorkflows.body: Test one scene idea with a clear subject, action, camera path and final pose.

referenceWorkflows.title: Image draft
referenceWorkflows.body: Preserve source identity and framing while specifying only the motion that should unfold.

referenceWorkflows.title: Audio-driven draft
referenceWorkflows.body: Choose a permitted source clip, state the visible performance, and align scene beats with its rhythm.

referenceWorkflows.title: Safe iteration
referenceWorkflows.body: Use owned media, avoid deceptive likenesses, and reject malformed anatomy, unwanted text or unsafe content before reuse.

tabs.label: Brief
tabs.title: Write the smallest useful scene
tabs.description: Define a subject, action and final beat that fit the duration.
tabs.copy:
Subject:
[Appearance and one protected identity detail]

Setting:
[Place, time and lighting]

Action:
[One visible movement]

Final beat:
[How the subject and camera settle]

tabs.label: Motion
tabs.title: Test camera and physical response
tabs.description: Use specific movement instead of generic energy words.
tabs.copy:
Camera:
[Static, track, push, pull, jib or focus shift]

Subject timing:
[Start, acceleration, pause and finish]

Environment:
[Fabric, hair, shadow, liquid or particles]

Continuity:
[Details that may not drift]

tabs.label: Audio
tabs.title: Plan audio-to-video input
tabs.description: Let source duration and rhythm define the visual performance.
tabs.copy:
Source audio:
[Owned asset and validated length]

Rhythm map:
[Opening cue, central accent and closing cue]

Visible performance:
[Movement linked to those cues]

Avoid:
[Unrelated cuts, identity changes, logos, captions and unsafe imagery]

tabNotes.body: Fast iteration works when the scene is small enough to compare across several controlled variants.
At 1440p, 4K or higher frame rates, keep the planned duration inside the active schema ceiling.
Audio-to-video uses the trusted source duration for billing and should not be described as a text-mode audio toggle.

globalPrinciples: Keep one primary action per short draft.
Use the same prompt skeleton when comparing motion variables.
Choose resolution after the creative question is clear.
Confirm source rights, consent and brand safety before attaching media.
engineWhy: Fast supports a broad native resolution ladder for iteration and review.
Dedicated text, image and audio modes prevent one ambiguous workflow from hiding required inputs.
A longer maximum on supported Fast settings gives draft sequences room when high-tier constraints allow it.

demo.title: LTX 2.5 Fast motion study
demo.prompt: Animate the supplied editorial still of a cyclist waiting beneath a concrete overpass. The rider looks left, shifts weight onto one pedal, and starts forward as the camera makes a gentle parallel track. Preserve the jacket, bicycle frame, face and wet pavement reflections. Keep background traffic soft and end with the cyclist crossing the brightest patch of light.
notes: The prompt protects source identity while asking for one readable action.
A single lateral camera move makes draft comparison easier.
